subject: mathematics

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.80 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 93.2. The book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages (unlike its LAQ/SAQ pages): the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Appearance years are the book's, board-split. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find both sets — what each notation means, and the values.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Double each image
steps.margin_note: One mark. 2f multiplies each image by 2 — do not confuse it with 2 + f, which adds.
steps.memory_tip: 2f MULTIPLIES each image by 2. Do not confuse it with 2 + f, which adds.

recall.must_convey: That each image is multiplied by 2, giving {(1,4), (2,−6), (3,−2)}, with the inputs unchanged.
accept: multiply each image by two so one four two minus six three minus two
two f doubles the second coordinate of every pair
the outputs double and the inputs stay
prathi image ni two tho multiply cheyyali
two f is one comma four two comma minus six three comma minus two

steps.why: 2f and 2 + f are different operations on the same set, and the paper asks both. Reading the notation correctly is most of the mark.
common_mistakes: Adding 2 instead of multiplying, which is the previous question.

steps.label: Square each image
steps.margin_note: The second mark. f² squares the IMAGE, so every value comes out positive.
steps.memory_tip: f² squares the IMAGE, so every value comes out positive.

recall.must_convey: That each image is squared, giving {(1,4), (2,9), (3,1)} — all positive, because squaring kills the signs.
accept: square each image so four nine and one
f squared is one comma four two comma nine three comma one
squaring makes the negatives positive so nine and one
prathi image square chesthe four nine one
the squares of the images are four nine one

steps.why: f² means the image squared, not f composed with itself — a real ambiguity in notation that this question is testing.
common_mistakes: Reading f² as fof, the composition, which is not what is asked.

insider_note: 2f doubles each image while f² squares it, so the two answers differ wherever the image is not 0 or 2. Squaring makes every image positive, and that is the quick visible check.
